newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges end week firm, cargoes weak.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges end week firm, cargoes weak.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges ended the weak on a positive note while cargoes seemed weaker with little buying interest, traders said.
High sulphur barges were talked late at $86/$87 a tonne fob Rotterdam after earlier trading a few times at $87, up to $2 higher than deals done on Thursday.

Demand was reportedly a little firmer than a day earlier at about 15,000 to 20,000 tonnes. One player was seen trying to push up the market to sell its own material at a good price, some traders said.

High sulphur cargoes seemed a little weaker with no buyers seen for two cargoes of bunker grade material offered at $79 fob and $81 fob respectively. The asking price on the latter had been lowered from $82 over the past two days.

But Russian material fetched a good price on Thursday with a U.K major said to have bought a 45,000 tonne cargo of E-4 at three means plus $2.65, or 15 cents a tonne higher than a deal for E-4 earlier this week.
One percent was quiet with buyers and sellers still far apart in the low and mid nineties respectively.
